question: Could the public record have predicted the 2026 NSSTS winners?
answer: Only partly: in 4 decisions made between February 10, 2026 and July 9, 2026, the public record named the serious field beforehand in 2 (for example 5 contenders, 2 picked), but the package rates 1 case strong and 3 partial, and in none could it single out the winners.

items.title: QTIME project-call selections
items.sub: QTIME additive-manufacturing inspection and qualification · decided February 10, 2026
items.text: The outcome supports the importance of NDI, transition-user and standards roles, but the nonpublic applicant field prevents a true winner-selection test.
kv: Honeywell International Inc.; Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation; Applied Science & Technology Research Organization of America; RTX Technology Research Center; ASTM International
Additive-manufacturing NDI capability; Transition-user participation; Standards and qualification role; America Makes access
Treat this as a recall test for the selected role types, not evidence that public signals could rank the applicants.

items.title: Space Data Network Backbone prototype delivery order
items.sub: Space Data Network Backbone · decided May 26, 2026
items.text: The public capability and acquisition record would have made SpaceX a strong candidate, but the undisclosed applicant and evaluation field prevents a calibrated probability or winner claim.
kv: Operating proliferated-LEO constellation; Optical-mesh capability; Vertical launch access; National-security acquisition access
The case tests whether operating-scale architecture and same-customer access outperform generic commercial-relay adjacency; it does not validate exclusive-winner scoring.

items.title: PTS-G design pool to Swarm 1 production selection
items.sub: Protected Tactical SATCOM modernization portfolio · decided June 9, 2026
items.text: The public evidence correctly bounded five serious design-pool participants but did not disclose enough technical, price or evaluation evidence to distinguish the two production selectees without false precision.
kv: Viasat, Inc.; Northrop Grumman Systems Corporation; Astranis Space Technologies Corp.; Intelsat General Communications LLC; The Boeing Company
Viasat, Inc.; Intelsat General Communications LLC
Same-program design order; Protected-SATCOM capability; Spacecraft or payload delivery path; Exact SSC program-office access
A fame-weighted model could have overpromoted Boeing or Northrop; the typed program-position model preserves all five until the production object arrives.

items.title: JLWS parallel prototype OTA awards
items.sub: Joint Laser Weapon System · decided July 9, 2026
items.text: The model would have placed both later awardees in the serious field, but the complete evaluated field and company-level award values are not public.
kv: nLIGHT DEFENSE Systems, Inc.; Lockheed Martin Aculight Corp.; General Atomics; Dynetics, Inc.
nLIGHT DEFENSE Systems, Inc.; Lockheed Martin Aculight Corp.
Direct high-energy-laser source or integration experience; Prior HELSI, IFPC or Navy prototype access; Scaling and beam-control evidence; Federal prototype pathway
The result rewards direct laser-system evidence over general defense-prime scale, while preserving General Atomics and Dynetics as nonselected public-path controls.
